_readme: Apps that don't fit the generic "one app image + optionally one database" shape generate-templates.js handles. Each needs a hand-authored docker-compose.yaml, verified the same real-deploy way as every other template — see the main README. isBespoke: true is a marker for tooling/UI that lists templates, not a schema generate-templates.js reads.

apps.reason: ~10 containers (Postgres, GoTrue, PostgREST, Realtime, Storage, Kong, Studio, ...).
Multi-container (MariaDB, Redis, InfluxDB, Telegraf, ...) plus a CLI init step.
No official plain docker-compose support — ships its own launcher/bootstrap tooling instead.
Web, worker, ClickHouse, Kafka, Redis, and Postgres — not a single app+db pair.
Two public services (builder + viewer) sharing one Postgres.
Storefront and admin are two separate public services.
Server plus an optional Dashboard — two public services.
Framework you build your own project with — no generic pre-built image exists.
Needs Postgres AND ClickHouse, not a single optional database.
Needs Postgres AND Redis; the generator only supports one backing service.
Needs Postgres AND Redis, and hard-requires S3-compatible storage — no local-disk mode.
No generic docker image exists at all (strapi/strapi was archived on Docker Hub in 2024) — same class of problem as Payload CMS, not fixable with a compose file.
Needs Postgres AND Redis; confirmed via a real deploy crash (createStandaloneRedisConnection failed with no Redis configured).

Neither invoiceninja/invoiceninja (php-fpm only) nor invoiceninja-debian is self-contained despite Docker Hub marketing suggesting the latter bundles nginx. The real official compose needs 4 services: app (php-fpm), a separate nginx container with a custom vhost config file, mysql, and redis. Confirmed via two real failed deploys, not assumed.
